one_line_contribution: A causal clause-by-target portability matrix for GEPA-discovered prompts, used to claim that a clause's value on its source task does not predict its cross-task value while a cheap seven-way clause-type label does, and to assemble a zero-rollout library of high-portability clauses priced in cold-start GEPA rollouts.
closest_prior_work: Self-Discover (Zhou et al., 2024) already ships a fixed library of domain-general reasoning modules that are selected and composed per task with zero task-specific optimization, which is exactly the artifact and the deployment story of Experiment (7); PromptBreeder (Fernando et al., 2023) likewise carries a reusable pool of domain-general 'thinking styles' and mutation prompts across tasks. Neither is cited. Together they largely pre-empt the loop-closing contribution (a reusable text library of domain-general prompt components beats nothing and costs no rollouts), leaving the genuine delta as the *measurement* — harvesting components from what an optimizer actually found and estimating their transfer causally. On the attribution machinery, prompt-compression and context-attribution work (LLMLingua; ContextCite, Cohen-Wang et al., 2024) already does leave-one-segment-out and regression-based marginals over prompt/context spans, so the estimator is not new either; only its application to optimizer-discovered clauses across tasks is. The proposal's distinction from SPoT/ATTEMPT ('soft prompts have no clause structure') is correct but is the modest-delta move the track brief explicitly warns is scored as a domain swap.
strongest_objection: The central dissociation is close to definitionally true, so confirming it carries almost no information. Prediction (c) says task-specific-content clauses show mean cross-task delta <= 0: a clause containing HotpotQA entity vocabulary or GSM8K arithmetic scaffolding, appended verbatim into an MBPP prompt, is simply off-topic text, and 'off-topic text does not help and sometimes hurts' is already the settled finding of the prompt-sensitivity literature the proposal itself cites. Nothing in the design isolates whether clause *type* predicts transfer over and above plain topical relevance: the mixed model in (6) controls for source contribution and clause length but not for any measure of clause-to-target semantic relevance, and the domain-scrubbed condition — the one manipulation that could separate 'type' from 'topicality' — is demoted to an ablation rather than being the primary contrast. Strip that away and the paper's one non-trivial claim is (d), the rollout equivalence, and that number is the most fragile quantity in the design: it is obtained by inverting a cold-start budget curve sampled at 0/10/25/50/100/300 with a measured per-run SD of ~3 points, so the 10-50 rollout region of the curve is flat within the proposal's own noise floor. If cold-start GEPA at 25 rollouts is not separable from 0 rollouts, then 'the library is worth 25-75 rollouts' is a statement about an interval of the curve where nothing is measurable, and the bootstrap CI on the inverse map will plausibly run from 0 to the whole budget. The proposal predicts a CI excluding zero and also predicts a low Spearman correlation, i.e. it stakes its headline on a null it is underpowered to distinguish from noise and a point estimate it is underpowered to bound. A secondary but real hole: split-half reliability across GEPA seeds is the linchpin of the attenuation correction, yet different seeds return different prompts with different clause sets, so it is unclear which clauses even have two measurements to correlate — beyond the near-duplicate-merged subset, the reliability estimate is undefined and the attenuation correction unfalsifiable.
what_would_fix_it: Three changes. (1) Make relevance, not type, the thing type must beat: add clause-to-target semantic similarity (and the domain-scrubbed variant of every clause) as primary conditions rather than ablations, and require the mixed model's DeltaR^2 >= 0.15 to survive after relevance is entered as a covariate — that turns a tautology into a real test of the 'two kinds of text' theory. (2) Drop rollout equivalence as the headline and replace it with a pre-registered fixed-budget contrast the design can actually resolve: library-seeded GEPA versus cold-start GEPA at 25 and 50 rollouts, paired per target, with the target count raised from 8 to at least 16 clusters so the leave-one-target-out claim has more than eight independent generalization units (the '24 paired observations' figure treats three seeds within a fold as independent, which they are not; the effective n for a cross-domain claim is 8, and the stated ~1.5-point sensitivity is correspondingly optimistic). (3) Add the LLM-distillation baseline below, and actually run the preprint search. Also trim: the ablation list (position x3, granularity x3, single-type libraries, 1-vs-7 sources, second executor, plus a full library-as-seed budget curve) multiplies the ~330k headline generations several-fold and does not fit the stated one-node, few-hundred-dollar ceiling as written.
missing_baseline: A zero-rollout, zero-measurement LLM-distilled prefix: hand the reflector model the seven source-task optimized prompts and ask it to write a generic, domain-general prefix of matched token length. This is the baseline that prices the paper's entire expensive apparatus — the ~168k-generation clause x target matrix exists only to rank clauses by measured portability, and if a single frontier-model call over the same source prompts produces a prefix that matches the harvested library on held-out targets, then the causal portability estimation bought nothing and the contribution collapses to the attribution study alone. The plan has a human checklist written blind (iii) and whole-prompt warm start (ii), but neither tests this: (iii) never sees the optimizer output, and (ii) transfers one prompt whole. Secondarily missing, and specifically named in the track brief: a task-similarity retrieval baseline in the SPoT/ATTEMPT spirit — pick the single nearest source task by embedding and reuse its prompt — which is the standard cheap way to get cross-task transfer and which the proposal cites as related work without implementing.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and the Related Work section states outright that all citations are unverified because the literature-search backend was unavailable. By the standard applied here that is a substantive weakness, not a neutral: the proposal asserts that no prior work attributes optimizer gain to parts of the returned prompt or measures those parts' portability, and it has run zero searches to support that assertion. The claim is also implausible on its face for a 2025-2026 submission — prompt-component attribution, prompt compression by span importance, and reusable domain-general instruction libraries are all active arXiv areas, and GEPA itself (cited as 2025) is recent enough that follow-up analyses of what its returned prompts contain are exactly the kind of preprint that would appear within months. At minimum the authors must search for and address: recent work decomposing or ablating optimizer-produced prompts; Self-Discover-style and PromptBreeder-style reusable domain-general component libraries; Shapley/leave-one-out attribution over prompt spans; and any cross-task prompt-component transfer study posted since GEPA. Until that search exists, novelty here is asserted rather than established, and I have scored it accordingly.
